fr.R: En ce temps-là, du vin doux coulera des montagnes, et du lait coulera des collines. \q L’eau remplira tous les ravins secs de Juda. \q Une source sortira du temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} \q et arrosera la vallée de Shittim.

sw.L: Na itakuwa katika siku ile [kwamba] milima itadondosha divai tamu, na vilima vitatiririka maziwa, \q na mabonde yote ya vijito vya Yuda yatatiririka maji; \q na chemchemi itatoka katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} \q na kulinywesha bonde la Shitimu.
sw.B: Siku hiyo milima itadondosha divai tamu, na maziwa yatatiririka kutoka vilimani; \q mabonde yote ya vijito vya Yuda yatajaa maji yanayotiririka. \q Chemchemi itabubujika kutoka nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} \q na kulinywesha bonde la Shitimu.
sw.R: Wakati huo divai tamu itadondoka kutoka milimani, na maziwa yatatiririka kutoka vilimani. \q Maji yatajaza mabonde yote makavu ya Yuda. \q Chemchemi itabubujika kutoka hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} \q na kulinywesha bonde la Shitimu.

vi.L: Và sẽ xảy ra trong ngày ấy [rằng] núi non sẽ nhỏ giọt rượu ngọt, và đồi sẽ chảy sữa, \q và mọi khe suối của Giu-đa sẽ chảy nước; \q và một dòng suối sẽ tuôn ra từ nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} \q và tưới thung lũng Si-tim.
vi.B: Vào ngày ấy, núi non sẽ nhỏ giọt rượu ngọt, và sữa sẽ chảy từ các đồi; \q mọi khe suối của Giu-đa sẽ tràn nước. \q Một dòng suối sẽ tuôn ra từ nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} \q và tưới thung lũng Si-tim.
vi.R: Vào lúc ấy, rượu ngọt sẽ nhỏ giọt từ núi non, và sữa sẽ chảy từ các đồi. \q Nước sẽ chảy đầy mọi lòng suối khô cạn của Giu-đa. \q Một dòng suối sẽ tuôn ra từ đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} \q và tưới thung lũng Si-tim.

decisions.choice: the mountains will drip sweet wine: the words of Amos 9:13
decisions.reason: Amos 9:13 ends with the same picture: "the mountains will drip sweet wine". The sweet wine that was cut off in 1:5 flows freely. Milk and wine are signs of a land made rich again, like the land "flowing with milk and honey" (Exodus 3:8).

decisions.choice: a spring from the house of the LORD
decisions.reason: Ezekiel 47:1-12 sees a river flowing from the temple that brings life wherever it goes, and Zechariah 14:8 sees living water flowing out from Jerusalem. Revelation 22:1-2 takes up the picture of the river of life.

decisions.choice: the valley of Shittim: the valley of the acacias, its place uncertain
alternatives: the Shittim of Numbers 25:1, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Shittim means acacia trees, which grow in dry ground. The valley may be a dry valley running from Jerusalem towards the Dead Sea, such as the Kidron, or the name may stand for any dry, barren valley, now watered. Shittim was also the name of Israel's last camp east of the Jordan (Numbers 25:1; Joshua 2:1), but that is across the river.

decisions.choice: streambeds: watercourses that are dry for much of the year
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in 1:20 for the channels of water that had dried up. Now they all run with water.

decisions.choice: in that day (L); On that day (B); At that time (R); Shittim (all levels)
decisions.reason: The phrase follows the wording set in Isaiah. Every level keeps the name Shittim, with a footnote on its meaning and place (m3). Readable says "temple" for "the house of the LORD" and "dry streambeds" for the watercourses (m4).

decisions.choice: "el valle de Sitim"
decisions.reason: The name as Joshua 2:1 in Spanish; the meaning footnote explains it as the valley of the acacias.

decisions.choice: "los montes destilarán vino dulce" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Amos 9:13 has the same words, and the Spanish of both keeps one wording.

decisions.choice: "trong ngày ấy" (L); "Vào ngày ấy" (B); "Vào lúc ấy" (R)
decisions.reason: "In that day" follows the formula settled for Isaiah and Jeremiah at each level.

records.literal_gloss: Egypt to a desolation will become, and Edom to a wilderness of desolation will become, because of [the] violence [to the] children of Judah, whose innocent blood they shed in their land.

en.L: Egypt will become a desolation, \q and Edom \q a desolate wilderness, \q because of the violence [done to] the children of Judah, \q whose innocent blood they shed in their land.
en.B: Egypt will be laid waste, \q and Edom \q will become a desolate wilderness, \q because of the violence done to the people of Judah, \q whose innocent blood they shed in their land.
en.R: Egypt will become an empty wasteland. \q Edom will become a dry desert. \q This is because of the violence they did to the people of Judah. \q They killed innocent people in Judah's land.

es.L: Egipto se convertirá en desolación, \q y Edom \q en desierto desolado, \q por la violencia [hecha a] los hijos de Judá, \q cuya sangre inocente derramaron en su tierra.
es.B: Egipto quedará devastado, \q y Edom \q se convertirá en un desierto desolado, \q por la violencia que hicieron a la gente de Judá, \q cuya sangre inocente derramaron en su tierra.
es.R: Egipto se convertirá en un desierto vacío. \q Edom se convertirá en un desierto seco. \q Esto será por la violencia que cometieron contra la gente de Judá. \q Mataron a gente inocente en la tierra de Judá.

fr.L: L’Égypte deviendra une désolation, \q et Édom \q un désert désolé, \q à cause de la violence [faite] aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Juda, \q dont ils ont versé le sang innocent dans leur pays.
fr.B: L’Égypte sera dévastée, \q et Édom \q deviendra un désert désolé, \q à cause de la violence faite aux gens de Juda, \q dont ils ont versé le sang innocent dans leur pays.
fr.R: L’Égypte deviendra une terre vide et abandonnée. \q Édom deviendra un désert sec. \q C’est à cause de la violence qu’ils ont faite aux gens de Juda. \q Ils ont tué des innocents dans le pays de Juda.

sw.L: Misri itakuwa ukiwa, \q na Edomu \q jangwa la ukiwa, \q kwa sababu ya udhalimu [uliotendwa] kwa wana wa Yuda, \q ambao walimwaga damu yao isiyo na hatia katika nchi yao.
sw.B: Misri itaachwa ukiwa, \q na Edomu \q itakuwa jangwa tupu, \q kwa sababu ya ukatili uliotendwa kwa watu wa Yuda, \q ambao walimwaga damu yao isiyo na hatia katika nchi yao.
sw.R: Misri itakuwa nchi tupu iliyoachwa. \q Edomu itakuwa jangwa kavu. \q Hii ni kwa sababu ya ukatili waliowatendea watu wa Yuda. \q Waliwaua watu wasio na hatia katika nchi ya Yuda.

vi.L: Ai Cập sẽ thành một nơi hoang vu, \q và Ê-đôm \q thành một hoang mạc tiêu điều, \q vì sự bạo ngược [đối với] con cái Giu-đa, \q vì chúng đã đổ máu vô tội trong đất của họ.
vi.B: Ai Cập sẽ bị tàn phá, \q còn Ê-đôm \q sẽ thành một hoang mạc tiêu điều, \q vì sự bạo ngược chúng đã làm cho dân Giu-đa, \q là những người vô tội mà chúng đã đổ máu trong đất của họ.
vi.R: Ai Cập sẽ thành một vùng đất hoang trống trải. \q Ê-đôm sẽ thành một sa mạc khô cằn. \q Đó là vì sự bạo ngược chúng đã làm cho dân Giu-đa. \q Chúng đã giết những người vô tội trong đất của Giu-đa.

decisions.choice: Egypt and Edom: old enemies of Judah
decisions.reason: Egypt had invaded Judah and taken its treasures (1 Kings 14:25-26) and killed King Josiah (2 Kings 23:29). Edom, Judah's "brother", is accused of violence against Judah when Jerusalem fell (Obadiah 10-14; Psalm 137:7). The word for "violence" in Obadiah 10 is the one used here.

decisions.choice: the violence of the people of Judah: violence done to them
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the violence of the children of Judah", meaning violence that Judah suffered, as "the violence of your brother Jacob" in Obadiah 10.

decisions.choice: in their land: in Judah's land
alternatives: in the lands of Egypt and Edom
decisions.reason: "Their land" most likely means Judah's own land, where Egyptians and Edomites killed its people. It could mean the lands of Egypt and Edom, where people of Judah had fled.

decisions.choice: in Judah's land (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the land (m3).

decisions.choice: Judah will be inhabited forever: it will remain, full of people
decisions.reason: The verb means to sit or dwell; said of a land or city it means to be inhabited, or to remain in place (Isaiah 13:20; Jeremiah 17:25). Judah stands against Egypt and Edom, left empty in verse 19.

decisions.choice: But (all levels)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "and" introduces a contrast with verse 19, which every level marks with "But".

records.literal_gloss: And I will hold innocent their blood [which] I have not held innocent; and Yahweh dwells in Zion.

en.R: I will punish those who shed their blood, which I have not yet done. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} lives in Zion.

es.B: Vengaré su sangre, que había dejado sin vengar. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} habita en Sion.
es.R: Castigaré a los que derramaron su sangre, cosa que todavía no he hecho. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} vive en Sion.

fr.L: Et je tiendrai pour innocent leur sang [que] je n’ai pas tenu pour innocent, \q et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} demeure dans Sion.
fr.B: Je vengerai leur sang, que j’avais laissé sans vengeance. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} habite à Sion.
fr.R: Je punirai ceux qui ont versé leur sang, ce que je n’ai pas encore fait. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} habite à Sion.

sw.B: Nitailipiza damu yao, ambayo nilikuwa sijailipiza. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anakaa Sayuni.
sw.R: Nitawaadhibu wale walioimwaga damu yao, jambo ambalo bado sijalifanya. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} anaishi Sayuni.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ kể là vô tội máu của họ [mà] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chưa kể là vô tội, \q và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ngự tại Si-ôn.
vi.B: Ta sẽ báo thù cho máu của họ, là máu {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chưa báo thù. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ngự tại Si-ôn.
vi.R: Ta sẽ trừng phạt những kẻ đã làm đổ máu họ, điều mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} chưa làm. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sống tại Si-ôn.

decisions.choice: I will hold innocent their blood: I will vindicate the innocent blood of Judah by bringing the guilty to account
alternatives: "Shall I leave their bloodshed unpunished? I will not."
the Greek translation: "I will avenge their blood"
decisions.reason: The verb means to treat as innocent or to leave unpunished, and it plays on "innocent blood" in verse 19. Read with that verse, "their blood" is the innocent blood of the people of Judah, and the LORD will at last declare it innocent by punishing those who shed it. The line is hard, and it has been taken in other ways: as a question, "Shall I leave their bloodshed unpunished? I will not"; or, following the Greek translation, which has "I will avenge", with a different verb. The sense is much the same in each: the LORD will not let the killing of his people go unanswered.

decisions.choice: the LORD dwells in Zion: the book ends with God's presence
decisions.reason: The last words of the book say that the LORD lives among his people. Ezekiel's book ends in the same way: "the LORD is there" (Ezekiel 48:35).

decisions.choice: avenge (B); punish those who shed their blood (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew verb, "hold innocent". Balanced and Readable say what it means here (m1): the LORD will avenge the blood by punishing those who shed it.

decisions.choice: "je tiendrai pour innocent" (L)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one French renders "tenir pour innocent" in Exodus 34:7 and 20:7; Literal keeps it so the reader sees the Hebrew's wording, which Balanced and Readable explain as avenging the blood (the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "kể là vô tội" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew verb of declaring innocent, as the English Literal does; the meaning decision gives the sense that Balanced and Readable say outright.
